ai.description: *Leptobrachella tamdil* is a small frog (SVL 23–26 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring dark, irregular markings. It is distinguished by a granular skin texture and distinct, pale yellow toe tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Leptobrachella tamdil* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, large, irregular dark brown blotches on its flanks, which contrast sharply with its lighter belly.
ai.habitat: *Leptobrachella tamdil* inhabits evergreen forests in Mizoram, India, typically found near rocky, fast-flowing hill streams at elevations between 600 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: *Leptobrachella tamdil* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active near forest streams at night to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and mossy rocks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Leptobrachella tamdil* breeds in streams during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Leptobrachella tamdil* is endemic to Mizoram, India, specifically found in the Tamdil Lake area at elevations between 700 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Leptobrachella tamdil* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted by males residing near fast-flowing forest streams.
